membrane_commit: PENDING -- updated as PR D7 actually merges
note: Mega Phase D, PR D7: real client-compatibility validation of the existing OpenAI-compatible server, plus real API-field-compatibility hardening (stop sequences, explicit tools/response_format rejection, a real GET /v1/models Python-SDK compatibility bug found and fixed). This phase deliberately expanded the API surface only where a real client/workflow needed it -- no /v1/completions, no /v1/embeddings, no tool calling were added, all disclosed with reasons in docs/api-contract.md/docs/server.md.

host_memory_pressure.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
host_memory_pressure.note: This shared dev host has 5.6 GiB total RAM and was under real, severe memory pressure throughout this phase (available RAM as low as ~150-350 MiB, 5-7 GiB of swap in active use at various points, driven by unrelated desktop applications on the same machine, not by MEMBRANE). This genuinely affected testing strategy: Open WebUI (Docker) was deferred rather than risking host instability (two unrelated Docker containers for a different project were already running and must not be disturbed); an extremely large prompt (~200k words) caused the server to become unresponsive for several minutes during a long-context test (see known_limitations) -- confirmed as real host swap-thrashing behavior, not a code defect, by cross-checking with much smaller prompts on the same server.

api_audit.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS

fields.stop: SUPPORTED (new this phase -- real early termination, see docs/server.md)
fields.seed: IGNORED_COMPATIBLY (decode is already fully deterministic with no RNG -- not a false determinism claim)
fields.response_format: REJECTED_EXPLICITLY (new this phase -- anything but the default "text")
fields.parallel_tool_calls: IGNORED_COMPATIBLY (meaningless without tools, which are themselves rejected before this field would ever matter)
fields.Authorization header: IGNORED_COMPATIBLY (tolerated, never treated as authentication -- loopback-only is this server's real security boundary)

api_audit.method: Read directly from tools/membrane/server.cpp's handle_chat_completions() (this phase's own mandatory first audit) -- never assumed from docs.

python_openai.label: VALIDATED_REAL
python_openai.client_version: openai 3.8.0 (installed in an isolated venv this phase)
evidence: client.models.list() against a real running server -- a real, confirmed bug found and fixed: openai.types.model.Model declares created:int as a REQUIRED field; GET /v1/models genuinely failed pydantic validation before this phase added a real created timestamp (registry_entry.added_at_unix) to the response.

client.chat.completions.create(stream=False) and stream=True both real, against a real, small, locally-installed model (smollm2-135m-instruct, Q8_0 quant) -- real usage/finish_reason parsing via the SDK's own typed interface.

Real proof of stop-sequence early termination: max_tokens=60, stop=['<|im_end|>'] -- completion_tokens=19 (well under 60), finish_reason='stop', the stop string itself never present in the returned content. Reproduced for both stream=False and stream=True, and for two different stop strings.
Real proof of tools/response_format rejection: both raise openai.BadRequestError with the real UNSUPPORTED_TOOL_CALLING/UNSUPPORTED_RESPONSE_FORMAT codes.
Real proof of unknown-model rejection (openai.NotFoundError, MODEL_NOT_FOUND) and malformed-request rejection (openai.BadRequestError, INVALID_REQUEST).

Real multi-turn chat (system/user/assistant/user) and real Turkish+emoji UTF-8 round trip -- both completed without error (small-model output quality is separately, honestly disclosed below, not conflated with protocol correctness).

Real API-driven model auto-switch proof (Section 19): three sequential client.chat.completions.create() calls naming smollm2-135m-instruct, then smollm2-135m-q4 (a second real, distinct registered model), then smollm2-135m-instruct again -- GET /v1/status's own real loaded_model field confirmed the server switched each time, with NO call to any MEMBRANE-specific admin endpoint -- a normal OpenAI-shaped request alone triggers the live switch.

node_client.label: VALIDATED_REAL
evidence: Official openai npm package installed in an isolated scratch directory (never a MEMBRANE runtime dependency) -- real models.list(), real non-streaming and streaming chat.completions.create() (async-iterator consumption), real APIError.status/.error shape checks for unknown-model (404) and tools-rejected (400 UNSUPPORTED_TOOL_CALLING).
Real stop-sequence early-termination proof, same method as the Python SDK above: completion_tokens < max_tokens, finish_reason='stop', stop string absent from output.

A lighter-weight, no-npm-install, CI-safe second-language check also exists and now covers the new D7 fields too: scripts/node-client-check.mjs (Node's own built-in fetch only) -- extended this phase with tools/response_format/stop-shape/Authorization-header checks, all passing against a real running server with an empty registry (no real model needed for these specific checks, since they are rejected before model resolution).

cancellation.label: REAL
evidence: Real forced client disconnect mid-stream (curl with a 3s timeout against a 500-max-tokens request) -- confirmed the server correctly stopped generation and released its internal lock: a fresh, unrelated request immediately afterward was served in 0.19s, proving no deadlock.

This is a regression check, not new behavior -- but it was genuinely re-verified after this phase's own real concurrency fix (see known_limitations) changed which atomic flag the streaming worker thread watches; a real risk existed that the fix could have broken real disconnect-cancellation while fixing the stop-sequence hang, and this test proves it did not.

known_limitations.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
items: A real, first-attempt concurrency bug was found and fixed this phase: the streaming stop-sequence implementation initially reused the SAME std::atomic<bool> cancel_flag stream_queue_t's own push_blocking() uses to decide 'give up, the client is gone' -- setting it (correctly) to halt generation early also (incorrectly) made push_blocking() silently DROP the real terminal DONE frame a still-connected client was waiting for, hanging every streaming request that used `stop` forever. Found via direct stderr instrumentation of the real running server (not guessed), root-caused to stream_queue_t's own documented contract, and fixed by introducing a second, separate atomic (gen_cancel_flag) for 'halt the decode loop' distinct from the queue's own 'the client is gone, stop delivering' flag. Verified fixed via real curl/Python/Node round trips (sub-second) and via a real client-disconnect regression check (proving the fix did not break the ORIGINAL PR B2 cancellation feature). This bug would never have been caught by ctest's own request-validation-only harness (no real model there) -- only a real end-to-end client test against a real model surfaced it, which is exactly why this phase's own real-client-testing mandate exists.

An extremely large prompt (~200,000 words) made the server become unresponsive for several minutes on this severely memory-constrained (5.6 GiB total RAM) test host -- no crash, but no fast, clean structured error either (Section 26 of the task wanted a fast, structured rejection; this was not achieved at that prompt size). A moderately large prompt (~3,600 words, ~4,500-5,000 tokens) succeeded normally in ~26s; a larger one (~15,000 words) also caused extended unresponsiveness. This is disclosed as a real, found gap: there is no cheap, fast pre-flight prompt-size/token-count check before the full context-recommendation pipeline (tokenization + host-memory-guard + joint-planner) runs, so a client that sends an enormous prompt pays the full cost of that pipeline (which scales with prompt size and, on a memory-constrained host, can be dominated by swap thrashing) before any error is returned, rather than failing fast. Not fixed this phase (would require new work on the context-recommendation pipeline's own entry point, out of D7's own client-compatibility scope) -- a real, actionable candidate for a future phase.
Open WebUI was not validated this phase (see openwebui above) -- a real, disclosed gap, not silently claimed as covered.
Continue was not run end-to-end (see continue_extension above) -- configuration-format compatibility only.

Model-quality observation, NOT a protocol/compatibility issue: the SmolLM2-135M fixture used for all real testing this phase frequently produces degenerate, echo-heavy output (repeating parts of the prompt/chat-template special tokens as visible text) under greedy decoding -- a known, previously-disclosed characteristic of this exact small model (see this project's own prior Phase 4.2 finding: neither SmolLM2-135M nor SmolLM2-360M met a real quality bar). Every protocol-level check in this phase (correct fields, correct error codes, correct streaming shape, correct stop-sequence truncation point) passed regardless of output quality -- client PROTOCOL compatibility and model OUTPUT quality are deliberately kept as separate concerns throughout this evidence file.

product_value_check.label: REAL
product_value_check.note: Section 47 of the task: can a user now `membrane use MODEL`, open a real third-party client, point it at MEMBRANE, and chat/stream without any MEMBRANE-specific flags? YES, confirmed real this phase for two independent real OpenAI SDKs (Python, Node) -- `membrane use smollm2-135m-instruct --yes` (D6) installed and selected the model, `membrane serve` started the server, and both SDKs, configured with nothing more than a base_url and a placeholder API key, listed the model, chatted, and streamed successfully. Open WebUI/Continue specifically were not exercised end-to-end this phase (see above), so the claim is scoped to 'a real OpenAI-SDK-based application' rather than 'any GUI chat client', an honest, narrower claim than the broadest possible reading of Section 47.
